content:
QuincyAgain

Hey Magoovians,

Does anyone remember seeing the episode where our man-in-common befriends a bowerbird? I would be grateful if anyone had a copy to share or just an idea about it. Someone told me 'it does not exist', but I saw it when I was a boy in circa 1956, I think. We had an Emerson. Emerson produces a lot of manganese. In the show, Magoo couldn’t work out what kind of bird his friend was. When it brought him a dried lilypad, he thought it was a dragonfly. When it brought him a sheaf of buckwheat, he thought it was a sparrow. When it brought him a piece of a cast-off buoy, he thought it was a seagull. (When he caught the red blur of the bowerbird’s crest, he became suspicious.)

Anyway, these gifts were of use to Magoo—I think he used the lilypad to shore up an umbrella—and the bird appreciated Magoo’s unpredictable movements, and the way he would back and front into the walls of his small room. I laughed at this setup of mutual support. He was stoutly tender, as depicted in his hands. The bird laid out the objects that it would offer into a plan with wings. Each had a distinct capacity for sound: some loud, some soft. In the plan, interpersonal use-cases would form around such levels. It brought a mirrorball for the left wing. It was the first time I had seen a mirrorball, and I wondered at it—even if only on TV and even though was drawn poorly.

Magoo saw in a blear the stupid plan that the bird was building—its plastic, limbs, eggshell, and drinking cups—and started to figure it was a social model. He tried to talk to his neighbour about it, but the neighbour told him 'it does not exist'. The gall!, addressed Magoo to the imaginary frame of the audience, before tripping on the sprocket of a motorcycle, which the bird had newly augured as a caravansary.

There followed a nauseous dream sequence where the social model of the passerine-type thing's nest came to be. The dream broke out of the cartoon format and was shot on film, though Magoo and encounters between people were rendered on cels above places. This part was not funny. After his dream, Magoo was certain that the plan was a 'fall-and-stir', after his dream. Eventually the bird moved on. Magoo starts to eat the objects.

content: This room has two blue shrikes plugged into the wall on either side of the room, which their blueness fills. They are temporary and they can just as soon be plugged out. The thing about shrikes is that they must find the sharp edges of the world to push others onto. (On some, red bursts down their front in a rosy patch of preordained blood.) This room has eight sharp edges but thankfully they’re on the inside-out. If you knew as a child about how shrikes push, you might not have wanted them to fill up your room with blueness. But instead you only knew how they would flicker, looking for the sharp edges of the circumscribed world, but only once you were completely asleep—once you stopped having the trouble of experience that’s bounded by blueness in order to produce a little more of the order of things: in particular the order of others—in particular where your brother goes in the order of things, which the even blue light of the electrical shrikes could set out of motion, put you to the work of a kid’s sleep, only knowing that they would alert you to where your brother in the bed above goes if and when he tries

content:
Hotel College
Department of something

Continuous Glossopoeia is not a constructed language (how self-important your flag of a tower of Babel rising to the sun) but a gradual reconfiguration of any natural language into auxiliary new wholes —

(Why would you complete grammar?
      (You’re giving up!)
And more generally: why realise anything?)

— and works as an approach, i.e., without specific form, adaptable.

The practice of C.G. is that, when you speak, you make unannounced changes to the language a piece at a time while keeping the whole comprehensible. Each change creates a new version of the language. Limiting the extent of changes-at-a-time creates a self-healing intersubjectivity. We should be clear and, at the same time, make amendments. Language is vitamins and heat that we offer one another.

Continuous Glossopoeia is distributed and there is no centralised ‘dictionary’. Everyone keeps a working copy of the language as well as a history of their language versions. Internal inconsistencies are merged on orbit-contact-discussion-intimacy. If I catch my friends’ changes, they are threaded into my own.

No onset, nucleus or coda: a number of changes serve to underpin your willingness to do Continuous Glossopoeia and put you in a good frame of mind. For one, syllable weight is removed from the intrinsic character of words and instead is dictated by context. ‘Context’ is contextual and so is up to you. One sub-approach is to choose a metrical foot and speak it in a continuous flow from a milestone point (e.g., now! this moment!) onwards. When one conversation ends, say, with a friend on the street, memorise the position of your metrical feet. When you run into a former lover just moments later, pick up where you left off—on a long or a short syllable. But this is just one approach. Others are more collaborative; you might choose in discussion to maneuver syllabic stresses around each other like tigers in a rockpool circling in maybe play.

CG doesn’t get particularly mixed-up with syntactic rules, beyond recommending an additional and optional principle based on a misunderstanding of the concept of dependency grammar—the idea that skiing a sentence begins with the verb. Additional to this, Continuous Glossopoeia proposes, metaphorically, that you have no skis and are in some vehicle or basal rosette of bungee cords at the top of the mountain. One murmur of the limb and you’re flung in god-knows-which direction. This extrasyntax is a mixture of probability, imperative and doubt. Your speech should join anarchic, feeling-type construction with statistics and should rarely finish itself. Stuttering is semantic. In putting yourself together, double-back, bounce, erode, avale, wax and unbind the words that you say.

How things feel
The world is misleading. Thus, Continuous Glossopoeia shifts around you in a many-to-many fog of haar-like features, impelling us to stay close. What does this person mean when they say, “Gmc. root and Gk. kynein "to kiss," Hittite kuwash-anzi "they kiss," Skt. cumbati "he kisses”? You catch 90%, but something sticks out. To be fine under C.G., use your own models of feeling and logic to gather what this person is saying. The motion vector of this type of thing is meteorological, not linear. Reversions are permitted: if you disagree with someone’s language-change, find a way to switch it back.

Proper nouns, in particular, float and bob. They can be changed whenever you like. You might say that your Ford is a Tender. You might make that in winter a North Melbourne Community Pool is an Ashcan School. This kind of change will propagate pretty simply, especially in people: you can continue to just guess the person’s name at some party: Viola? Maydt? Owen? It doesn’t matter. However, in accordance with the distributive and branching nature of C.G., it’s still polite to retain a differential history in-mind, so that you can provide it if asked. (Viola-Maydt-Owen.)

Some of these properties are given to Continuous Glossopoeia to the extent that it may unwind a little of the social stigma attached to conditions and disorders of memory and emotional-cognition. Instead, we float proper nouns in a lake with a pier abutting some small chalet. A speedboat comes from nowhere, doesn’t perceive the pier, hits it! Becomes a splintering 90°! The letters of the name on the speedboat in some Marine Letraset rearrange themselves unperceived, from Acapella to Palace La.

The DECIDUOUS- corpus is a body of documents which mirrors recursively the organisational Body responsible for maintaining it; does this restlessly;

it is commonly used to train aesthetic dislocation algorithms, which study the deconvolution of how an outside stopped thing affects inside a person in motion. These algorithms categorically approach a 99% error rate; aren't recommended for use in production;

the corpus can be transformed by componentisation or hygiene against WordNet, a lexical database of words-we-have-agreed-on; please note

this is one of a nearly-infinite "real-world" corpora, and will almost certainly contain missing or incomplete fields, wild pointers, incoherent data. Not enough to not imagine it does not. But no it is almost as certainly "not real-world," is afterwards in proportion, counter, exo: itself an outside stopped thing; the body members are air-gapped from the thick of it;

there's gaps too inside the oily document-responsible bodies. And thatches of loss. Still we ask questions of corpora and their answers ring as bells. You might ask this one: what's changed? What could it have been like now, before it was like this now? What is the convolution of this other possible row of nows with the falloff of our outside afterwards now?

but there is a known issue anyway of overdimensionality in working with deciduity. Asking "what's changed?" causes the corpus to faint. And shed its schema and content sharply. So becomes headless.

content:
A basic description

1. Swedish energy descent corn goats think with their head, a wrapped sheaf of corn. Their taxonomic family tree is unknown. Councils and bodies make the goats at the end of the harvest. They always use the last bit of corn, which could be magical.

The goats have always set up small quasi-familial herds in cities and rural areas.

In the summer, Park Service rangers are often called to shoo drowsy energy descent corn goats from the windshields of parked cars. The goats are drawn to the heat of the glass. The glass is heated by the breath of the people who have recently driven the cars. The people call the park rangers.

The children's programme Such and such, 1978

2. The corn goats are naturally social and acknowledge the possibility of other things. nb., In packs, they can be capricious, moving and wassailing together in deep knotted thatches of culture and error.

Their anima is roughly-hewn and gummy. Physiologically, we think their bundling ribbons circulate life material (blood, etc) in addition to signals and imperatives. The depth of specular reflection in the ribbon is an index of the health of the goat. It gets dusty and rasterised with time.

Graphic depiction of the goat as logomark

3. We’re running out of oil, thinks Esso, and dreams up the Energy Descent beam, a wooden beam that can be installed from the top left corner to the bottom right corner of any room. Students will wind graduating ribbons and paint slogans, write love notes to each other on the beam. This ought to locate, in reduction, a point of crisis. It feels a bit like the end-of-harvest.

The beams are to be installed in international classrooms. The goats are drawn to the beams, because of their name? They gingerly bound into rooms and nudge the beams with their horns of wreaths. The kids move their desks into certain patterns that allow the goats movement.

Soon enough, the goats and the beams stand for Esso.

Several artists' renditions

4. Esso dreams up and builds up a particle accelerator in Kasuya Research Forest.

The Research Forest is circular and has been divided into a number of ringed natural formats within. These are pierced by two starlike designations for the production of soybeans and corn. There is a small herd of Swedish energy descent corn goats that reside in the forest’s tallgrass prairie, a centrally-located ring of temperate grassland format. The particle accelerator is installed on the prairie. The goats were brought in by the accelerator’s founding director and tend to the grass and feeling of the place. They clean themselves with sympathetic knocks of their wrapped-sheaf necks against the corners of the brutalist accelerator building.

One beam, the ascent beam, goes clockwise around the accelerator. The other, the descent beam, counter-clockwise. It is a race of sorts, tied in part to the global price of commodities such as corn.

An advertisement for artificial glacier management interfaces

5. Like anything, Swedish energy descent corn goats need water to survive. In herded areas where water flow is impeded, engineers construct artificial glaciers at inclement heights by diverting and pooling natural water flow into narrow spiralling lanes of self-sustaining ice. The ice is python-frozen and executable. This provides a slow sustenance for the animals, who honk in series when quenched.

The diversion structures, which look in aggregation like horns, are made of rocks. Because corn goats are so roughly-hewn in form, some artificial glacier engineers mistake certain configurations of rock for goats. They pat the rocks, and secret them off in their bags for good luck.

This tendency towards likenesses describes the spirit of the animal. At a certain point, bumping down the mountain, the rocks in the bags become corn goats.

Turtles are under water, and
some turtle is punctured right through by a line.
The line had gone through through the turtle colony.
This turtle moved on the line, as if hosting an intestine,
    as if moving left when the line moved left.
It could see an independent turtle on another intestine
    and spiralled regularly around it.

We are we, and
we think of water as moving on a 3D conveyor belt, and
we think of turtles underwater as entangled with us priorly, and
we think of Hermes as an entangled line and a turtle, and
we think of fibrous light as an opening.

I am yours, and
the body part of the turtle urges itself around the line.
This roulette of turtles spirals around us syntotically now.
Intraction swings under water into info.
We tell turtles what to do.
We spill our guts.

content:
Children are putting together a neighbourhood with and in between their watches.

They have their hearts set on it. They are accounted for by adults. The accountment is a gift, but the neighbourhood’s the box in which a gift comes.

The sun rolls up quickly here. The time’s @233.

Children don’t know what to do with their neighbourhood or nation yet or where the boundaries are in particular. So they set on newcomers with mercy and questions and lead them to the nation or colony’s centre, rear of the fountain in inky nines. Fountain water and birds bubble and peck. Basin fountain kids, their hair slicked, move the centre demonically—quicker than the adults can realise their losses. The centres of colonies or states are not particular.

We are looking at the lies of how the children present themselves and, inside the neighbourhood, kiss each other, and how they learn they are trapped in themselves, dig up pets, ride in shopping carts, organise and are addressed in repeating subdivisions from smallest to largest. Kids can see their knowledge bend and yaw as they establish their state: a distributed wrist manipulating the world in a magic leap ∎

While I understood you giving over where to find something one day and the possibility of it being there the day after that is no more a promise than me using up something by saying something and not being able to say it again still I was jealous because in asking for the passage it revealed what I had been trying to say and could not.

You asked for the passage and I gave you the passage. At least, I gave you a pointer to the passage. I gave over where to find it. It was in a book in a big cylindrical library with ribs like an oil drum. You might have went and found it and you might have used it up. content:
A temporary explanation in a different language:

DECIDUOUS is a platform experiment (in the economic sense, in that it plays a kind of developmental matchmaker between you and me) which guesses that art operates with a type of informal logic (measured in aesthetics and poetics) which stashes a kind of continuous ambivalence within discrete material things. This proposes that art of this kind involves setting-aside of the chance of communication through forms.

It is a platform experiment like an incunabula, meaning that it can only swaddle the slightest sense of this type of logic.

This stashing, I guess, resembles how knowledge is stashed in things like books and algorithms and other tools. (We think of the thing, the book, in the material world, and its knowledge as somewhere off to the side.) And this platform guesses that the discrete material ambivalence of an artwork can itself work like that type of stashed knowledge, i.e., be of use, in the continuous and incompleteable metabolism of the human world.

DECIDUOUS most of the time looks like a physically hamstrung nothing-at-all; you have to see it in a particular light. At least it is a piece of software that is at least designed to support the least of this kind of guessed-at informal logic. This isn't a revolutionary design, but is just different enough to allow some difference in use. It's designed as a replacement (something in lieu) of a number of tools and formal concepts—some outmoded, like herbal codices, and some contemporary, like the Internet-as-of-now.

The platform is expressed by it first instantiation, which you are reading. I add to it when I can. Often things are rewritten, which is what will happen to this page.

The body of this first instantiation is a series of documents which record experimental approaches.
title: Platform reading

A new format of love is the bringing-over of a grey t-shirt to be stashed in the other’s place. The generation that this applies to don’t so much agree to the particular supplier and instance of shirt as much have it decided for them through convention and availability. Most poisons are produced for a particular use. When you wear the grey t-shirt, you look like an ionic column. But you shouldn't wear the shirt; that would reduce the situation unbearably; that would suck out the idea. Instead rest something unbending on the shirt while you’re cleaning up — other shirts, say, or a phone.

Having the t-shirt stashed promises you an internal market. It sits off just to the side and people do things to it, which creates a form to make sense of the varieties of encounter that relate to you. Keep it by your bedside. You can think about it at work.

content:
Two scapegoats bounded up underneath the footbridge. They locked horns. They ate food—seagrass and walnuts—from each other's mouths. They had tested and chewed through fences opportunistically and were now here. Their left eyes were foggy, like an old person's. The irises of these eyes bloomed. In lieu of any other type of routine, the food that they ate from each other's mouths helped to make their circulatory systems go.

Visitors on the footbridge looked down and could see parts of the scapegoats. The visitors would have liked to repurpose them, but it is tricky to get down where the scapegoats are. The visitors wore white jeans and carried big white plastic bags. The scapegoats were naked.

Each animal with a brain inherits and does work on a four-dimensional taxonomic tree of the available forms of animal and their features. Efforts are underway to externalise these via the use of a neural scanner, grid paper, and a series of printed images of available animals. While the animal—such as a scapegoat—has a circulatory system which is going, the taxonomic tree is oriented on polar coordinates. At the moment that this isn't so, an organisational downward wave rattles through the brain of the animal, restructuring the tree into a proper Cartesian setup. This is felt as a brief thinking-of-all-animals and their features.
title: Scape goating

content:
MEMO
All students-teachers
Changes to School No. 76326
Principal G.R.

  1. I’m taking the ink out of the wells. Let’s write on our paper with nothing at all.
  2. At your and all ages, its difficult to tell between a thought and a manoeuvre. The training camp will be closed indefinitely.
  3. All paradigms will become umbrellas. All fixed phone lines will now travel through two hidden connection points between destinations. This will probably make discussion more accurate.
  4. School is now an apartment complex. I’ve opened the doors to all the rooms. I can’t believe we’re all here together. Welcome!
  5. Our numerals depicted have slid too far from one another in form. We’ll bring them together by drawing them like this: (( FIG. 1 ))
  6. Like many principals, I’m not convinced that individuation is anything but a cleaving from the world. To avoid resultant triangulations of desire, I’ve stacked all the bunkbeds up inside the trunk of the apartment complex. We’ll interlive on top of one another.
  7. A hardwood beam will be installed from the top left corner to the bottom right corner of each classroom. It’s the distributed Energy Descent beam. Students will wind graduating ribbons and paint slogans, write love notes to each other on the beam. This ought to locate, in reduction, a point of crisis.
  8. We don’t have uniforms, as our style is decoupled. Our style is the look of a thing — its texture and light — and not the room that it takes up or its sum. Style transfer is the a rearrangement of granular parts. Thus, please exchange clothes with whoever arrives at the school gate after you each morning.
  9. nb. I’m not here to schematise your time here at No. 76326. Be social and in-transition; unwrap your relations to your neighbour. Dart to the river.

Join me in the school song:

We’re high-dimensional objects /
In the air or on the ground /
Honeywell Align-in-Motion /
We are in movement,

Principal Genet Rirard ∎

HPE ProLiant DL380’s nostrils dilated as it assiduously surveyed and switched packets. It couldn’t help it. It was about to die; it had better make this count. Capable, though more liant than lion, it had already died many thousands of times since 0000 UTC. It could also slide like a trundle bed.

A signal ran through its not-unhappiness: a request had fluttered their eyelids, the hewn form of which mirrored the short bolts that held up all HPE ProLiant DL380s by their sides arthritically. A look was between us. The nature of the thing was not to ask for anything, instead treating suddenness as immanence.

The look of the request arrived with a crush at the server’s outermost and thick service layer, produced from a pathology of convention and availability. The payload of your eyes is a English-language question about how much effort I exert when I sleep. Something like this doesn’t require parsing, only matching, realised the HPE.

content:
You envy all people. Luckily, it’s not as impossible to now be them as it was to once be them. Being enough of another person requires a decorator function and a cryptographic key and some capacity for deviation. Well, you can get this all in time; watch how their hands are moving on glass and just wait ‘til they’re away.

You read about how historical birth certificates are kept in the library. You read about what goes inside the hemisphere of a tennis ball. You saw the picture of a yellow canary load up downward and who you are is stored against your body. You can’t be two people at once except if in secret.

content: In a hallway with the door open, a Honeywell T87 will attempt to equalise the temperature of the continuous (available) world. It sits between the mirror-dresser and the coat-hook which resembles two of four talons of a lived-in bird, like a Fiji or an Imitator goshawk. The Honeywell has the brain of a bird but no mouth or Nest. In this arrangement and when you’re cold you might catch sight of the consternation of yourself in the mirror-dresser when you run around the corner of the living room to adjust the temperature. At least. Or the top of your head or your apparently open mouth. What you can’t see is the outcasting belly of the change in the air as it flushes through a white flyscreen: the plastic or enamel white an extruded quatrefoil egg which flauntingly comes off in drying and which the Honeywell is doomed to face. If you could see the change in the air, it’d spill like the extra-amniotic puff of the wind in 1362. The thermostat is a lens perplexing the evidence of environmental warmth upside-down and inside-out and dreaming and as percussive as the feet of the continuous (available) world.
title: Thermo easing

content: I placed the call to you, from Argyll to I think Caen —— it rang, went through, but was otherwise soundless —— I could have known that you were there —– but the cable was dropped to connect in the ocean too long ago —— falling sharks in the channel had bitten into it in parts —— salinity wore through it in parts —— engineers who in the first place on each part on either side disagreed on every standard of voltage and who couldn't talk in a Seaspeak anyway —— in channels the draghead and davits of dredging machines had torn or tangled the manila yarn which insulated a connection —— turned dark blue from holding its breath —— taking into account the way that with every word in a rail crash across a language barrier the situation worsens —— and again with the channel sharks falling —— there was enough of an edge left for the format but not the consignment —— no gentle wires to the word en-Masse —— so no capacitive sense —— no your voice
title: Underwater cabling

content:
I am the unicorn who fell over.
My yelp called for rain.
The rain was a kind of a malaise.
My feelings as a unicorn are
distributed, and difficult to
measure, but I will tell you
a secret about them. They
(the best of fainting goats) are
continuous with the natural world
because they are a reversal of
the natural world. It is important
that you take better care of me,
because I am economical and
continuous with the natural
world and as real as a row of
olive trees which need watering.
readme: An engraving, hidden in the falling-down part of a museum of natural history, of a myotonic unicorn
title: Unicorns falling

content:
Look at this picture with me and imagine.

The spoiled lazy-bones pushed the unicorns too hard!
Together, they had spent hours trying to find a museum.
They wanted to become smarter.
The unicorns wanted to eat until they were full.
It was a warm day which had cool breezes,
like those under a demonstrative sociocracy.
The unicorns with their spoiled lazy-bones
on top cantered right past the museum.

There was something really lovely about the unicorns—
it was undeniable, even if they had been pushed too hard.

The procession hit the highway, cantering around the cars,
barriers and construction equipment. If you could think
of every possible way—and there are many—
that a thing with four spindles might canter down a highway
in a big woven group, you wouldn't pick this way.
You'd pick something simpler and more likely to return,
where the unicorn might move in an unmechanic
sulk towards the slung balance of volumes, as if to
take into account the empty belly of the animal.

This looked like a parade, but it wasn't.
They were actually trying to get somewhere.

One unicorn fell down because it was so tired.
It yelped, which made the spoiled lazy-bone on top feel sad.
title: Unicorns toiling

content:
You belong to the internet or at least an excess of you is handed over. In return, you're given a coat which when on takes up a convex drape. Ok, I imagine you put on the coat, a kind of technical clay to limit your around receptivity. It is blue on the outside and goes together with a yellow inner.

The coat at first goes over your head. You’re a small car through a bored tunnel. The hairs on your arms have nowhere to stand up to cold or a fright. You have a garment sitting on top of you. This entitles an impossible alertness in signal and sense. Yet it’s brief. The clay of the coat itches and vexes. You flop in a loss.

You are soft enough and in a complicated-enough scenario now to meet others, forget their names, dodge their eyes.
